rachel: quick heads-up — strict mypy fails in the python SDK for streaming chat responses in the async sample app.

rachel: Repro: generated stub says `def chat_stream(...) -> AsyncIterator[dict]:` but runtime yields ChatResponse objects. mypy/pyright both complain when code expects attributes.

rachel: Example:```py
async for msg in client.chat_stream(...):
    print(msg.text)  # mypy: "dict" has no attribute "text"
```

tom: hmm. Is the generator defaulting to dict when response schema is a union or when streaming mode is enabled?

nikhil: I dug in — template uses the "to_native" fallback that returns dict for streaming endpoints. We should prefer the model class type when we have a defined model.

liu: also seeing a pyright variant where the type becomes `AsyncIterator[Union[ChatResponse, None]]` because of nullable fragments in the response shape. That union triggers a bunch of downstream type nastiness.

rachel: ugh. Workaround for customers: `from typing import cast, AsyncIterator` then `stream = cast(AsyncIterator[ChatResponse], client.chat_stream(...))` — gross but works.

tom: we should: 1) change generator to emit AsyncIterator[ChatResponse] when model exists, 2) ensure Optional[...] wrapping for nullable pieces, 3) add `from __future__ import annotations` to generated files so forward refs aren't required inline.

nikhil: agree. Also add TYPE_CHECKING guards: `if TYPE_CHECKING: from .models import ChatResponse` and otherwise import lazily or use string annotations. Minimizes runtime import cost.

liu: minor: pydantic v2 parse return types are weird (sometimes `Model | None`). That affects the inferred return type in templates. We should normalize to `Optional[Model]` in stubs.

rachel: created a tiny failing unit test that runs mypy+pyright against the async quickstart and asserts the stub contains "AsyncIterator[ChatResponse]". attaching snippet to the issue.

devx-bot: Issue #5010 created by @rachel (area: python-sdk-typing, priority: high).

nikhil: plan: patch generator to prefer model classes for streams, wrap nullables with Optional, add future annotations import, and add CI jobs for pyright+mypy. I'll open a PR and include tests.

tom: thanks. can we also update the README sample to use a typed example so onboarding customers don't hit this? small docs patch helps immediate UX.

rachel: will update sample README meanwhile.

devx-bot: PR #5016 opened by @nikhil: fix(python-gen): proper streaming return types + mypy/pyright regression tests. CI queued. :rocket:

liu: after PR lands, let's run a quick beta with the onboarding customer to validate.

rachel: agreed. thanks all! :heart:
